1.1.0.lead: nexbeat can now request from nexcrate as well, and from this version on this window tells you after each update what changed.

sections.title: Requests to nexcrate
sections.body: Where there was only Lidarr, an administrator can now choose nexcrate. Nothing changes for you: request as usual and follow the state under My requests.
sections.where: Menu at your name › My requests

sections.title: About nexbeat
sections.body: Version, licence and this text now live at the bottom, under “About nexbeat” in the footer. You can open this window again from there.

sections.title: Update hint
sections.body: Once a day nexbeat asks GitHub whether there is a newer version and shows it in the footer and on the page. It can be switched off on the same page.

small: When nexcrate refuses something, its own reason is shown below.
After connecting to nexcrate the library is there at once.

1.1.1.lead: Two repairs: requests to a slow nexcrate, and artists who share a name.

sections.title: Requests to a slow nexcrate
sections.body: When nexcrate took longer than a minute to answer, nexbeat showed error 504 although the request had arrived, and sent it a second time in the background. nexbeat now hands a request over in the background and never sends the same one twice at once. Until nexcrate has taken it, the request says "Handing over".
sections.where: Menu at your name › My requests

sections.title: Artists who share a name
sections.body: Artists of the same name all got the photo and the top tracks of the best known one. Both now come by the artist's MusicBrainz entry, and search tells namesakes apart by country and description.

1.2.0.lead: nexbeat now has API tokens. With one, dashboards like nexdeck show your requests, and administrators approve requests right from the dashboard.

sections.title: API tokens
sections.body: In your profile you create tokens for scripts and dashboards. A token has exactly your rights; ticked “Read only” it can neither request nor change anything. It is shown once, sent as the header Authorization: Bearer … and can be revoked at any time.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › API tokens

sections.title: nexbeat in nexdeck
sections.body: With a token nexdeck shows waiting, running and failed requests, the library and, for administrators, the requests to approve with buttons to approve and turn down. The buttons need the token of an administrator that may write.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › API tokens

sections.title: Who has which tokens
sections.body: Under Users you see which accounts created tokens and when they were last used. Only its owner can revoke a token; deactivating an account locks its tokens too.

small: Changing your password leaves tokens working. Revoke the ones you no longer need in your profile.
The interface for your own scripts is under /api/v1 and described at /api/docs.

1.3.0.lead: You can now sign in through authentik, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Authelia, Pocket ID and any other OpenID Connect provider. nexbeat sets up authentik by itself in one click.

sections.title: Sign in with your provider
sections.body: The sign-in page has a button for every provider that is set up. If you already have an account, link it once in your profile; after that you can sign in without a password. Whoever joins through a provider can set a password of their own there later.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › Sign-in providers

sections.title: authentik in one step
sections.body: With the address of authentik and an API token, nexbeat creates its provider and application there and adds itself as a sign-in provider. The token is used for this only and is not stored. If you would rather not hand over a token, download a blueprint instead.

sections.title: Add a provider yourself
sections.body: Any OpenID Connect provider can be added by hand, Microsoft Entra ID with one or many tenants included. For each provider you decide whether new accounts are created on first sign-in, and with which role.

small: Accounts are matched only by the provider's ID for a person, never by email address. An existing account gets to a provider only through the link in the profile.
A provider through which accounts without a password were created can only be deleted after a confirmation.

1.4.0.lead: Signing in through a provider is now the same in every nexbeat app: several providers side by side, a safer return to the app, and a question before the public address changes.

sections.title: Invitations through a provider
sections.body: The invitation page now has a button for each provider. Whoever follows an invitation continues with their provider and comes in with the rights the invitation carries. Linking an existing account in your profile asks for your password once more.
sections.where: Menu at your name › Profile › Sign-in providers

sections.title: Three cards for sign-in
sections.body: Settings now show the sign-in with its public address, the list of providers in the order of the buttons, and the authentik step. Password sign-in can be switched off once a provider is active; administrators can always use their password. Changing or clearing the public address asks first when a provider knows it, because the return address of every provider changes with it.

sections.title: New accounts are always members
sections.body: People who join through a provider become members, also where 1.3.0 had set another role for that provider. The rights of an administrator come only from an invitation. Providers set up in 1.3.0 keep working and keep their return address.

sections.title: Behind a reverse proxy
sections.body: nexbeat takes the scheme (http or https) of a request only from the proxies named in the setting FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (default 127.0.0.1, comma separated, * for all). Behind a proxy that ends TLS, add its address there. Nothing else was needed before, so check this after the update.

small: The session cookie now lives under /api so the return from a provider sees who is signed in. You may have to sign in once more after the update.
Mails now carry a Date header; large mail providers had dropped them without a word (issue #2).
API tokens, for example for nexdeck, keep working unchanged.

1.4.1.lead: A small repair release: nexbeat now trusts no proxy until you name it.

sections.title: Trusted proxies are empty by default
sections.body: FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS used to default to 127.0.0.1. It is now empty, so nexbeat takes the scheme and the sender of a request from no proxy until you add its address (addresses or networks such as 172.16.0.0/12, comma separated, * for all). With a bridge network, as on most NAS, nothing changes. If nexbeat runs with host networking behind a proxy on the same machine, add that proxy there, otherwise the session cookie loses Secure and the authentik card warns.

1.4.2.lead: nexbeat now fits on a phone, and Deezer is off by default.

sections.title: On a phone
sections.body: Long titles and addresses no longer push the page past the edge, buttons and links are big enough for a finger, and input fields no longer zoom in on the iPhone. Thanks to francescoferruccio for the contribution.

sections.title: Deezer off by default
sections.body: Artist images and previews from Deezer are now off by default. If you never saved that source yourself, it is off after this update too. To get images and previews back, switch Deezer on again under Sources.

small: On a phone, a single button in the header switches between light and dark.

1.5.0.lead: New from your artists: what came out in the past month is now on the start page.

sections.title: New from your artists
sections.body: A new row on the start page shows albums and EPs from the past 30 days by artists already in the library, newest first, with the release day. What is already there or downloading is marked, everything else can be requested as usual. The list comes from ListenBrainz. Thanks to xkevinx for the suggestion.

small: When the browser translates the page, for example Chrome or Edge, nexbeat now keeps working. Before, the page could go blank when you clicked a button.

1.6.0.lead: When you request a whole artist, you now choose which kinds of albums come, when nexbeat requests from nexcrate.

sections.title: Album types for a whole artist
sections.body: When you request a whole artist, the dialog lets you choose the types: studio albums, EPs, singles, live albums, compilations, soundtracks, remixes, spoken word or other, several at once. Studio albums are preselected. Future albums of these types follow on their own. This works when nexbeat requests from nexcrate; with Lidarr its metadata profile still decides. Thanks to luiscarrasco2324 for the suggestion.
sections.where: An artist's page › Request the whole artist

sections.title: What is preselected
sections.body: You decide which types the dialog preselects. Out of the box it is studio albums.

small: If an artist is already in nexcrate, a request no longer takes a type away there. Before, every request set the artist to studio albums only, and future EPs stopped coming.
For whole artists, the request lists show which types were requested.

1.6.1.lead: Two fixes: New from your artists no longer shows other people’s compilations, and linking a provider keeps the cursor in the password field.

sections.title: New from your artists
sections.body: If Lidarr lists “Various Artists” as an artist, every new compilation showed up in the row, whoever it was by. Various Artists and placeholders like “[unknown]” no longer count as your artists there. Thanks to xkevinx for pointing it out.

sections.title: Linking a sign-in provider
sections.body: In the password field, the cursor jumped to the Link button after every letter. Now you type your password in one go.
